public_health_question.v: How did CDC's risk mitigation strategy and permit process for importing dogs from Egypt during the 2019–2020 suspension operate, and did it prevent rabid dog importations?

ev.q: Consultation with subject matter experts enabled CDC to develop a risk mitigation strategy that permitted 296 dogs to be imported from Egypt
None of the 296 dogs developed rabies after importation.
Review of CDC’s Suspension of and Advance Written Approval Process for Dogs Entering the United States from Egypt
Applications were uploaded and stored in CDC’s Quarantine Activity Reporting System (QARS), a secure database that records CDC’s border public health activities

equity.level_reason: The units are imported dogs and their permits; no human social-position dimension is analyzed. Importer affiliation (military, State Department, contractors) is administrative, not framed as social position.

notes: Design is a program review of a CDC import permit process; no tests or CIs. Dog rabies vaccination is an animal vaccine, so vaccine_outcome_type is null. Comparison led by the processing-time pair; Table 2 also shows monthly counts side by side.
view_issues: Table 1 percentages do not match counts for some ports (JFK 105 shown as 36.8%, ≈35.5%; Seattle 7 shown as 2.7%, ≈2.4%). Text says 42% short-term travelers; Table 1 gives 42.9% for travelers in Egypt <1 year. Table 2 '2019 total' cell has a stray period.
